metadata.title: Why CrowdStrike and cybersecurity stocks got crunched in Thursday’s rout - MarketWatch

content.text:
Tech Stocks
Why CrowdStrike and cybersecurity stocks got crunched in Thursday’s rout
Highflying cybersecurity names take a beating from broader market concerns as well as ‘Black October’ infrastructure hacks and news about AI disruptors
Cybersecurity names were once seen as a resilient corner of the software sector, positioned to benefit from the artificial-intelligence boom instead of being disrupted.
But as a widespread selloff gripped tech stocks and broader markets on Thursday, cybersecurity companies were feeling the heat as well. Shares of CrowdStrike CRWD and Okta OKTA fell around 10%, while Cloudflare NET dropped 8%. Palo Alto Networks PANW fell 9.6%. These declines were significantly steeper than the 4.4% loss posted by the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF IGV.
